title: A Salt for the Choir
premise: Cyrus Galloway, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the ivory he carves, has spent his life as the invisible ledger-keeper of the Guild of Impossible Things, trading in relics, oaths, and souls. When the old gods stir and begin answering prayers again, Cyrus learns that a soul he sold years ago to save his sister—the soul of his first love, Wren—now anchors the usurper's claim to the court beneath the mountain. To free Wren and break the usurper's divine mandate, Cyrus must abandon his anonymity, rally the guild's outcasts, and descend into the mountain court before the usurper's armies swallow the free cities. He succeeds at terrible cost: Wren is restored but mortal and changed, the guild is burned to its foundations, and Cyrus, half-deaf from the gods' answering, chooses a small life with her among the living rather than the power he was offered.
about_author: Lior Nystrom is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing guild records in northern port cities before turning to fiction. They write quiet, ledger-obsessed fantasy about people who keep other people's secrets for a living.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Cyrus Galloway balances the guild's ledgers in the free city of Vellmark, carving a dead sailor's last words into whalebone while ignoring the voices only he can hear. A routine audit reveals an entry he doesn't remember writing: his own name, dated tomorrow. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: uneasy comfort shattered by first dread.

chapters.title: What the Ivory Remembers
chapters.summary: Cyrus traces the anomalous entry to a soul-bond contract signed in his own hand seven years ago—Wren's soul, sold to the court beneath the mountain. His mentor, Guildmaster Ossen, warns him to burn the page. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: Across Vellmark, old shrines crack open and forgotten gods answer prayers—a baker's blight lifted, a drowned child returned wrong. The guild's impossible trade surges. Cyrus hears the dead singing in unison for the first time. POV: Cyrus, with a brief interlude from shrine-keeper Maren. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Tithe
chapters.summary: A herald arrives demanding the guild surrender its registry of soul-contracts to the usurper Ashkaval, whose armies march on the free cities. Ossen refuses; the herald leaves a tithe-mark burned into the guildhall door. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the guild's invisibility ending; duty pressing in.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Lost
chapters.summary: Cyrus secretly copies every soul-contract, hunting Wren's original deed. He finds it sealed with a god's sigil—meaning the sale was witnessed by something divine, making it nearly unbreakable. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: determination hardening against despair.

chapters.title: Maren of the Cracked Shrine
chapters.summary: Shrine-keeper Maren, whose god answered her prayer by taking her voice, joins Cyrus, able to read the god-sigils he cannot. She reveals the old gods are waking because someone beneath the mountain is feeding them prayers like kindling. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: two broken people finding alliance.

chapters.title: The Guild of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Ossen convenes the guild's scattered members: a forger of memories, a debt-collector of promises, a cartographer of places that don't exist. Cyrus proposes stealing back Wren's soul; half refuse, fearing the usurper. POV: ensemble, anchored in Cyrus. Emotional beat: fragile fellowship formed.

chapters.title: Ashes on the Ledger
chapters.summary: Usurper agents torch the guildhall archive. Ossen dies shielding the master registry, pressing it into Cyrus's hands with the words 'you were never invisible.' POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: grief and inheritance—the ledgers become his burden.

chapters.title: Road Beneath the Pines
chapters.summary: Cyrus, Maren, the memory-forger Sable, and the promise-collector Hesk flee toward the mountain, pursued by tithe-marked hunters. Cyrus carves Ossen's dying words into bone and hears him clearly for the first time. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Burn Slowly
chapters.summary: In a refugee column, the party witnesses the war's human cost; a mother begs Cyrus to ask her dead son for forgiveness, and he does, weeping. Sable offers to forge Cyrus a new identity—an escape. He refuses. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: temptation of disappearance rejected.

chapters.title: Hesk's Price
chapters.summary: Hesk confesses he once collected a promise from Cyrus himself: silence about Wren's sale, paid for by an unknown buyer. The trail suggests someone inside the guild orchestrated it long ago. POV: Hesk. Emotional beat: betrayal within trust; the mystery deepens.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Door
chapters.summary: The guild's mapmaker opens a road that shouldn't exist, cutting weeks off the journey—but each traveler must pay with a true memory. Cyrus gives up his memory of Wren's face. POV: ensemble. Emotional beat: sacrifice made intimate and irreversible.

chapters.title: Footholds of the Old Gods
chapters.summary: In high passes, the party finds a waking god—a stone giantess half-asleep for centuries—who recognizes the god-sigil on Wren's deed: it belongs to the Mountain Below, the eldest god, now the usurper's prisoner-patron. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: awe; the scale of the conflict revealed.

chapters.title: Tithe-Marked
chapters.summary: Hunters ambush the party at a shrine. Hesk dies buying time, collecting one final promise: that Cyrus will not trade Wren's freedom for his own life. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: loss sharpening purpose; a vow taken.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Descending through drowned mines, they reach the subterranean court where Ashkaval's ancestors bargained with the Mountain Below. Souls hang in the vaults like lanterns. Cyrus finds Wren's light—dim, flickering, aware. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: reunion that breaks the heart.

chapters.title: Wren, Lantern-Bright
chapters.summary: Wren's soul speaks through the bone in Cyrus's pocket: she chose to be sold to shield him from a debt he never knew he owed. The Mountain Below has been keeping her as collateral for the guild's oldest contract. POV: interlaced Cyrus/Wren. Emotional beat: love revealed as sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Oldest Contract
chapters.summary: Sable deciphers the registry: generations ago, the guild sold the Mountain Below its own freedom, binding the god as the source of all answered prayers. Ashkaval holds the deed. Freeing Wren means voiding the contract—and unleashing or destroying a god. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the true stakes surface.

chapters.title: Audience with Ashkaval
chapters.summary: Cyrus trades himself—his hearing, his gift—for an audience, standing unseen in plain sight before the usurper, who wants the registry to legitimize his conquest. Cyrus stalls while Maren reaches the god-vaults. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: courage disguised as bookkeeping.

chapters.title: The Vault of Lanterns
chapters.summary: Maren gives her voice entirely to wake the Mountain Below, who shatters the vault. Souls rain free; Wren's light returns toward her body in the world above. Ashkaval's divine mandate cracks as his patron wakes angry. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: triumph bought with irrevocable loss.

chapters.title: A Salt for the Choir
chapters.summary: The awakened god offers Cyrus its power—to become the new anchor of answered prayers. Remembering Hesk's final promise, he refuses, offering instead the guild's registry so the god can settle its own accounts. The mountain accepts; the armies falter as their mandate dissolves. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: climax—power declined, self chosen.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: The free cities hold. The guild rebuilds in exile under new rules: no more soul-trade. Cyrus, half-deaf, relearns the dead's voices through touch alone. Wren, reborn mortal, remembers nothing but trusts the man who waits at her door. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: quiet grief braided with hope.

chapters.title: Entries in a New Hand
chapters.summary: One year later, Cyrus writes the first entry of a new ledger—not debts, but gifts returned. Maren teaches sign-language hymns to the waking god's new shrines. Cyrus and Wren plant a garden over the old guildhall's ashes. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: belonging found not in hiding, but in staying.
